description: Ferroelectric FETs built in the back end of line, using oxide-semiconductor channels that can be fabricated at low thermal budget on top of CMOS. Our twin-gate and dual-gate designs control the voltage distribution across the gate stack to break the usual trade-off between memory window and operating voltage.
title: BEOL-compatible oxide-semiconductor FeFETs

description: Stacking memory vertically to keep scaling density: 3D Fe-VNAND with a dual-layer oxide-semiconductor channel and a laminated ferroelectric stack, and dual-gate polarization-boosted charge-trapping flash for future 3D NAND.
title: Three-dimensional ferroelectric memory

description: Bias-temperature instability and device-to-device variability set the limits for real products. We design around them: a tri-layer stack that manages hydrogen to suppress positive and negative bias temperature instability, and a variability study of multi-grain ferroelectric switching.
title: Reliability of oxide-semiconductor transistors

description: First-principles calculations and quantum-transport simulations to design devices before they are built: from tunnel FETs based on two-dimensional covalent-organic frameworks to the modelling that guides our FeFET and charge-trapping flash experiments.
title: Computational design of nanoscale transistors
